fact: The Coulomb constant k is 8.99 times 10 to the 9 N m squared per C squared
The permittivity of free space, epsilon nought, is 8.85 times 10 to the minus 12 F per m
The permeability of free space, mu nought, is 4 pi times 10 to the minus 7 H per m
The elementary charge e is 1.602 times 10 to the minus 19 C
The electron mass is 9.11 times 10 to the minus 31 kg
The proton mass is 1.67 times 10 to the minus 27 kg
Charge is quantised as q = ne, where n is a whole number
Coulomb's law is F = k q1 q2 over r squared, an inverse square law, and it needs TWO charges because a force acts between two objects
The electric field is E = F over q = k times the MAGNITUDE of Q, over r squared, using only ONE charge, the one producing the field
Electric potential is V = kQ over r, a scalar, and note the plain r rather than r squared
Electric potential energy is U = kQq over r = qV, measured in joules
Work done is W = qV, that is charge times voltage
The field from the potential is E = minus dV/dr, or E = V/d for a uniform field between plates
Electric flux is Phi = EA cos theta, with theta measured from the normal to the surface
Gauss's law is Phi = Q enclosed over epsilon nought, counting the enclosed charge only
The field of a line charge is E = lambda over 2 pi epsilon nought r, falling as 1 over r
The field of a plane sheet is E = sigma over 2 epsilon nought, independent of distance
Inside a hollow conductor E = 0, because no charge is enclosed
The dipole moment is p = qd, in units of C m
The torque on a dipole is tau = pE sin theta, and it is zero when the dipole is aligned with the field
The energy of a dipole is U = minus pE cos theta, a minimum when aligned
Capacitance is C = Q over V, in units of farads
The capacitance of a sphere is C = 4 pi epsilon nought R, fixed by geometry alone
The parallel plate capacitance is C = epsilon r epsilon nought A over d, with epsilon r = 1 in vacuum
A dielectric gives C = epsilon r times C nought, and it always increases the capacitance
Capacitors in parallel add: C equivalent = C1 + C2 and so on
Capacitors in series combine as 1 over C equivalent = 1 over C1 + 1 over C2 and so on, giving less than the smallest
The energy stored in a capacitor is W = Q squared over 2C = one half CV squared = one half QV, three equivalent forms
Electric current is I = delta Q over delta t, and 1 A = 1 C/s
The work done by a battery is W = delta Q times epsilon, in joules
Ohm's law is V = IR, and 1 ohm = 1 V/A
Resistivity gives R = rho L over A, so long and thin means high resistance
Resistors in series add: R equivalent = R1 + R2 and so on
Resistors in parallel combine as 1 over R equivalent = 1 over R1 + 1 over R2 and so on, giving less than the smallest
Two resistors in parallel are R equivalent = R1 R2 over R1 + R2, that is product over sum
The voltage divider is V1 = R1 over R total, times V, with the wanted resistor on top
The current divider is I1 = R2 over R1 plus R2, times I total, with the OTHER resistor on top
Kirchhoff's current law is sum of currents in equals sum of currents out, which is conservation of charge
Kirchhoff's voltage law is that the sum of voltages around a loop is zero, which is conservation of energy
The Lorentz force is F = qvB sin theta, and it is zero if v = 0 or theta = 0
The full Lorentz force with both fields present is F = q(E + v cross B)
The radius of a circular path in a magnetic field is r = mv over qB, using v sin theta if the entry is at an angle
The cyclotron frequency is f = qB over 2 pi m, and it is independent of speed
The period of the circular motion is T = 2 pi m over qB, also independent of speed
The pitch of a helix is p = v cos theta times T, so cosine gives the pitch while sine gives the radius
The force on a current-carrying conductor is F = BIL sin theta, a maximum at 90 degrees
The magnetic dipole moment is m = NIA, for N turns of current I enclosing area A
The torque on a current loop is tau = mB sin theta = NIAB sin theta, and it is zero when m lies along B
The Biot-Savart law is dB = mu nought over 4 pi, times I dl cross r hat, over r squared: general but laborious
The field of a long straight wire is B = mu nought I over 2 pi r, falling as 1 over r
The field at the centre of a loop is B = mu nought N I over 2R, for N turns
Ampere's law is that the closed integral of B dot dl equals mu nought times the enclosed current, and it is used when the arrangement is symmetric
The field inside a solenoid is B = mu nought n I, where n is turns PER METRE, and it is uniform inside
The field of a toroid is B = mu nought N I over 2 pi r, where N is the TOTAL number of turns
Magnetic flux is Phi = BA cos theta, in units of webers
Faraday's law is emf = minus N times dPhi/dt, so it is the RATE OF CHANGE that matters
Motional emf is emf = BLv, for a conductor moving through a magnetic field
The self-induced emf is emf = minus L dI/dt, where the minus sign is Lenz's law again
The energy stored in an inductor is W = one half L I squared, mirroring one half CV squared for a capacitor
The transformer relation is Vs over Vp = Ns over Np, and it works for AC only
For emf and internal resistance, E = I(R + r) and V = E minus Ir, so V is always less than E
Like repels and unlike attracts, and everything electrostatic starts there
The hook for q = ne is that charge comes in coins, not in liquid: never a fraction of an electron
The hook for Coulomb's law is that tripling the distance drops the force to a ninth
E = kQ over r squared but V = kQ over r: the field is squared and the potential is not, because the field is a vector and the potential a scalar
Superposition means computing one contribution at a time then adding, and it works for forces, fields and potentials alike
Flux out equals charge in over epsilon nought, and external charges contribute nothing
E = 0 inside a conductor, because no charge inside means no field inside: the Faraday cage
C = Q over V is charge per volt, and it is fixed by geometry rather than by Q or V
The half in W = one half CV squared is there because the voltage climbed from zero as the capacitor charged
Capacitors add in parallel, which is backwards from resistors: remember one and flip it for the other
For V = IR, cover the one you want and the formula rearranges itself
The hook for R = rho L over A is that long and thin resists, while short and fat does not
A parallel resistance less than the smallest resistor is a free check on every parallel answer, and failing it means the reciprocal was not flipped back
Kirchhoff's current law is charge and the voltage law is energy: junctions conserve charge, loops conserve energy
A stationary charge feels no magnetic force because v = 0, and a charge moving along the field feels none because sin 0 = 0
Magnetic fields do no work: they steer but never speed up, so the kinetic energy is constant
There is no v in f = qB over 2 pi m, which is the cyclotron principle
CHANGE is the word in Faraday's law: a steady flux induces nothing
Lenz's law opposes, which is conservation of energy: nature always fights back
V = E minus Ir is why headlights dim when the engine is started
Step 1 of the seven-step method is to read the question twice and underline what is asked for, because many marks are lost answering a question that was not set
Step 2 is to list what you know with symbols and units, writing the unknown with a question mark
Step 3 is to convert everything to SI immediately, centimetres to metres and microfarads to farads, before anything else
Step 4 is to choose the formula containing what you know and what you want, and if none does you need an intermediate step
Step 5 is to rearrange in symbols first and substitute numbers only at the end
Step 6 is to compute, keeping the powers of ten separate from the front numbers
Step 7 is to check that the size is believable, the unit is right, and the sanity check applies
The seven steps are read, list, convert, choose, rearrange, compute, check, and steps 3 and 7 save the most marks while being the most often skipped
The ampere is the unit of current, one coulomb per second
An Amperian loop is an imaginary closed path chosen to make Ampere's law easy
Capacitance is the charge stored per volt applied, in farads
A conductor is a material in which charge moves freely, and an insulator one in which charge is bound and cannot move freely
The cyclotron frequency is the revolutions per second of a charge in a magnetic field, independent of speed
A dielectric is an insulator between capacitor plates, and it increases the capacitance
A dipole is two equal and opposite charges separated by a small distance
An eddy current is a loop of current induced inside a solid conductor by changing flux
emf is the energy per unit charge given by a source, measured in volts despite the name
An equipotential is a surface on which the potential is the same everywhere
The farad is the unit of capacitance, one coulomb per volt
A Gaussian surface is an imaginary closed surface chosen to make Gauss's law easy
Internal resistance is the resistance of a source itself, and it causes the terminal voltage to fall below the emf
A junction or node is a point where two or more conductors meet, and a loop is a closed conducting path
The ohm is the unit of resistance, one volt per amp, and ohmic means obeying Ohm's law with resistance constant at fixed temperature
Permittivity, symbol epsilon, is how readily a material permits an electric field, while permeability, symbol mu, is how readily it permits a magnetic field
Polarisation is the creation of induced dipoles in an insulator by an applied field
Resistivity, symbol rho, is a material's intrinsic opposition to current, in ohm metres
A semiconductor is a material between conductor and insulator whose resistance FALLS as it heats, and doping is adding impurities to make it conduct
A short circuit is a path of zero resistance, which carries all the current
A solenoid is a long coil of wire producing a uniform field inside, and a toroid is a solenoid bent into a ring
Terminal voltage is the voltage across a source while current flows, and it is always less than the emf
The tesla is the unit of magnetic flux density
A transformer is two coils coupled by mutual induction, which changes voltage and works on AC only
The weber is the unit of magnetic flux, one tesla square metre
The magnitude bars in E = k mod Q over r squared mean you drop the sign of the charge, because the formula returns the SIZE of the field while the sign of the charge fixes its DIRECTION instead
A field points away from a positive charge and towards a negative one, which is how the sign is used once the magnitude has given the size
Maxwell showed the speed of an electromagnetic wave is v = 1 over the square root of mu nought epsilon nought, which evaluates to 2.998 times 10 to the 8 m/s, exactly the measured speed of light
In an electromagnetic wave the fields are locked together by E = cB, and the wave satisfies c = f lambda
The plane wave solution is Ey = E nought sin(kx minus omega t) and Bz = B nought sin(kx minus omega t), where k = 2 pi over lambda is the wave number and omega = 2 pi f the angular frequency
The intensity of an electromagnetic wave is I = one half epsilon nought c E nought squared = E nought squared over 2 mu nought c = c B nought squared over 2 mu nought, in watts per square metre
The Poynting vector S = one over mu nought, times E cross B, gives the rate at which energy is transported per unit area
The energy density of an electromagnetic wave is u = one half epsilon nought E squared plus B squared over 2 mu nought, and because E = cB the electric and magnetic contributions are equal
